subject: Latency spike impacting HorizonPay checkout - cross-team coordination
messages:
From: Michael Chen <m.chen@horizonpay.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Checkout latency spike since 09:00 PST

Olga —

We started seeing a large spike in checkout latency this morning around 09:00 PST. Multiple customers reported timeouts and some transactions were retried by our frontend leading to duplicate charges for a handful of users. Our ops team captured traces (attached) showing long tail on tokenization and generation calls to your API. Can you confirm whether there are any platform-wide degradations? We need ETA for mitigation.

Thanks,
Michael Chen
Head of Integrations, HorizonPay
attachments: horizonpay-prod-traces_20261120.zip

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <m.chen@horizonpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Checkout latency spike since 09:00 PST

Team —

Thanks for the heads up, Michael, and for the traces. Assigning this as urgent. Quick context: HorizonPay is on Dedicated capacity in us-west with pinned model "rw-instruct-large-v2-q8" and burst route to hosted fallback. Impact appears localized to HorizonPay traffic but we need to verify whether this is a customer-side pattern or a platform routing/serving issue.

Immediate asks:
- Dev: can you triage whether this is kernel/backpressure/queue buildup on the us-west pool? Key things to check: recent kernel swaps, GPU memory pressure, batch queue length, and KV cache hit rates.
- Marissa: coordinate comms with HorizonPay and prepare a short mitigation note (what we know, what we’re doing, ETA). Avoid promising timelines >1 hour.
- Hannah: pull the SLO dashboard and token-level latency breakdown for the last 3 hours; attach graphs.

Attach any relevant traces/screenshots to the Jira (INF-2984) and cc me. I’ll own customer updates while engineering triages.

Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <m.chen@horizonpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Checkout latency spike since 09:00 PST

Olga / team —

Quick triage update (10:03 PST):
- Observed elevated tail latency on our us-west dedicated GPU pool starting ~08:55 PST.
- Root cause (preliminary): intermittent GPU driver retries after a rolling kernel update started at 08:45 by infra automation. A subset of worker nodes fell into repeated kernel-selection fallback which increased per-request setup time by ~400-900ms at the 95-99.9p.
- Impact: HorizonPay requests that hit affected nodes see ~1.2–2.5s increased latency per request; overall throughput reduced by ~8% on the pool during the window.

Immediate actions taken:
1) Removed the 4 affected nodes from rotation (drain + reprovision).
2) Forced a homogeneous kernel selection for the pool to avoid further fallbacks.
3) Increased autoscale headroom + temporarily relaxed the batch size cap for HorizonPay route to reduce queueing.

Next steps: complete node reprovisioning (ETA 35–45m), monitor KV cache warmup, and re-evaluate tail latency after nodes return. I’ve attached the kernel error samples and a short mitigation plan.

Attachments: latency-graphs-09-15-utc.png, proposed-mitigation-plan.md

—Dev (SRE Lead)

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Chen <m.chen@horizonpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Checkout latency spike since 09:00 PST

Michael —

Thanks for the trace dump — the team identified an infrastructure-induced tail latency (kernel selection/driver retries) affecting some us-west workers. Engineering has already drained the problematic nodes and is reprovisioning replacements. Immediate mitigations are in place (forced kernel selection and extra headroom on your route).

What we know now:
- Scope: impacts a subset of requests routed to a few us-west workers (not an account-wide outage).
- Visible effect: higher tail latency and a small throughput dip; root cause linked to automated kernel rollout.
- ETA: we expect normal tail latency to return within ~45 minutes as nodes reprovision and KV caches warm up.

What we’re doing next:
- Finalizing node reprovisioning and monitoring for regressions.
- Reviewing the automation rollout to prevent future mid-rollout fallbacks.
- Offering a one-time mitigative credit for any duplicate charges traced to retries (we’ll need a short list of impacted request IDs).

Marissa will follow up with a short incident note you can share with stakeholders. Please reply if you prefer a status call — we can do a quick 15-min sync.

Olga

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Chen <m.chen@horizonpay.com>, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Checkout latency spike since 09:00 PST — Incident summary

Michael —

Short summary for your stakeholders (can be forwarded):

Summary: Between ~08:55–10:10 PST on 2026-11-20 HorizonPay observed increased checkout latency caused by transient GPU driver/kernel-selection fallbacks in our us-west dedicated pool. Engineering removed the affected nodes and reprovisioned replacements; normal latency profiles returned once KV caches warmed (by ~10:10 PST).

Customer impact: increased tail latency for a subset of requests; ~0.03% of requests retried by the client which led to isolated duplicate transactions. Redwood is prepared to help identify affected request IDs and issue a one-time credit/adjustment if duplicates are confirmed.

Action items for HorizonPay:
- If you can share example request IDs or traces for the duplicate charges, we’ll prioritize reconciliation.
- Optional: enable short-term rate-limiting on client retries to prevent second-order duplicates while we finalize rollback safeguards.

Internal follow-ups (assigned):
- INF-2984: postmortem and rollout guardrails (Dev).
- Customer credit reconciliation (Olga + Billing).
- Automation change control: add preflight checks to kernel rollouts (Hannah + Infra).

Thanks for your patience — reach out if you want a deeper postmortem or a brief incident review.

—Marissa
Customer Reliability Manager
